x: Resistivity is measured in ohm-metre (Ω m), since ρ = RA/l. Ohm is for resistance and S/m is for conductivity.
t: Discriminate resistance, resistivity and conductivity units.

x: Current is charge flowing per second, so 1 ampere = 1 coulomb per second. Charge alone is in coulombs.
t: Recall I = Q/t.

x: One horsepower equals 746 W. 3.6 × 10⁶ is joules in a kilowatt-hour, a trap figure.
t: Recall 1 hp = 746 W.

x: One commercial unit of electricity is 1 kilowatt-hour, which equals 3.6 × 10⁶ J. kW is power, not energy.
t: Discriminate energy (kWh) from power (kW).

x: Option C is incorrect: nichrome is a high-resistivity heating alloy, while silver has the lowest resistivity of all. The other statements are true.
t: Recall silver as the best conductor and nichrome as a heating alloy.

x: Both are true and R explains A: a coil turning in a magnetic field has an induced emf, so mechanical work becomes electrical energy.
t: Check whether R is the principle behind A.

x: Both are true and R explains A: a current-carrying coil feels a torque in a magnetic field and turns, giving mechanical energy.
t: Check whether R is the principle behind A.

x: Both are true and R explains A: earthing gives leakage current a low-resistance path to ground, so it does not pass through a person.
t: Check whether R is the reason for A.

x: Both are true: a rectifier changes AC to DC and an inverter changes DC to AC.
t: Discriminate rectifier from inverter.

x: Statement A is true: metal resistance rises with temperature. Statement B is false: semiconductor resistance falls as temperature rises.
t: Discriminate metals from semiconductors.

x: I, II and IV are correct: a fuse uses the heating effect, is made of low-melting wire and melts at excess current. III is false because a fuse is connected in series.
t: Recall that protective devices are in series.

x: I, II and III are correct: generators, transformers and induction cooktops use electromagnetic induction. IV is false because wireless charging also works by induction.
t: Check each statement for the word "only".

x: A generator turns mechanical into electrical energy, a motor electrical into mechanical, a transformer changes voltage and a rectifier converts AC to DC, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the function of each device.

x: Three use the magnetic effect of current: motors, electric bells and electromagnets. A fuse works by the heating effect of current.
t: Sort each device by heating effect versus magnetic effect.
s:
How many of the following are applications of the magnetic effect of current?
1. Motors
2. Electric bells
3. Electromagnets
4. Electric fuse

x: Charge is in coulombs, the elementary charge is 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, one coulomb is 6.25 × 10¹⁸ electrons and esu and emu are other units, giving a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Recall 1 C = 6.25 × 10¹⁸ electrons.

x: All three are correct: small currents are in mA and μA, conventional current flows positive to negative, and electrons flow negative to positive.
t: Discriminate conventional current from electron flow.

x: All four are correct: voltage and emf are in volts, 1 V = 1 J/C, and resistance is in ohms.
t: Recall the units of electrical quantities.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: 1 Ω = 1 V/A follows from Ohm's law, while kΩ and MΩ are just larger multiples.
t: Check whether R is a reason or a side fact.

x: Resistivity is also given in Ω cm, conductivity is in S/m and equals 1/ρ, and conductance is in siemens, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Discriminate conductance (S) from conductivity (S/m).

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: G = 1/R is a definition, while the mho is just the old name of its unit.
t: Check whether R is a reason or a side fact.

x: Current is the same throughout a series circuit, voltage is the same across parallel branches, Kirchhoff's first law makes the junction sum of currents zero, and in parallel the current divides in inverse proportion to resistance, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall what stays constant in series and in parallel circuits.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Series connection
(b) Parallel connection
(c) Kirchhoff’s first law
(d) Current division in parallel connection

List-II
(i) Current is the same through all components
(ii) Voltage is the same across all components
(iii) Sum of currents at a junction is zero
(iv) Inversely proportional to resistance

Select the correct answer using the code given below.

x: Both are true and R explains A: in series the total voltage is the sum of each drop, so it divides among the components.
t: Check whether R is the rule behind A.

x: Both are true: parallel components share the same voltage, and Kirchhoff's second law makes voltage drops round a closed loop sum to zero.
t: Recall Kirchhoff's two laws.

x: Rubber is an insulator with very high resistivity. Silver and copper are conductors, and silicon is a semiconductor.
t: Classify each material as conductor, semiconductor or insulator.

x: All three are correct: power is in watts, kW and MW are commercial units, and 1 kW = 1000 W.
t: Recall the units of power.

x: All three are correct: 1 kWh is a 1 kW device running for 1 hour, which is 3.6 × 10⁶ J, and electricity bills are charged per kWh.
t: Recall 1 kWh = 1000 W × 3600 s.

x: All five use the heating effect of current: irons and heaters, filament bulbs, coil stoves, fuses, and electric furnaces and welding.
t: Recall heating-effect applications.
s:
How many of the following are applications of the heating effect of current?
1. Electric irons, heaters, geysers and toasters
2. Incandescent bulbs
3. Electric stoves with heating coils
4. Electric fuses
5. Electric furnaces and welding

x: Motors drive fans and EVs, galvanometers and meters measure current, loudspeakers and microphones serve communication, and tapes and hard disks stored data, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall applications of electromagnetism.

x: All five are correct: a fuse protects against overcurrent, melts at once in a short circuit, is used in mains and branch circuits and inside appliances, and prevents wiring fires.
t: Recall the role of fuses.

x: Both are true: earthing holds the metal body at zero potential, and in a fault the current runs to earth and blows the fuse; the earth wire is green or green-yellow.
t: Recall earthing and wire colour codes.

x: A generator works by Faraday's electromagnetic induction, a changing flux gives an induced emf, its parts are armature, magnets, slip rings or commutator and brushes, and it can be AC or DC, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iv, d-iii.
t: Recall the principle, parts and types of a generator.

x: A generator takes in mechanical energy of rotation and gives out electrical energy. A motor does the reverse.
t: Discriminate generator from motor.

x: A motor works by force on a current in a field (Fleming's left-hand rule), has armature, magnets, commutator and brushes, takes in electrical energy and gives out rotation, giving a-i, b-iii, c-ii, d-iv.
t: Recall the principle and parts of a motor.

x: Both are true and R explains A: mutual induction needs a changing flux, which only alternating current provides.
t: Check whether R is the condition behind A.

x: All four are correct: a transformer has primary and secondary coils on a soft iron core, works on AC because flux changes, and fails on DC because flux becomes steady.
t: Recall why transformers need AC.

x: Both are true: inverters supply AC for appliances in UPS units, solar systems and battery backups.
t: Recall the uses of an inverter.

x: Silver, copper and aluminium are good conductors with very low resistivity. Nichrome, constantan and manganin are high-resistivity alloys.
t: Classify each material by resistivity.

x: Both are true and R explains A: excess current heats the fuse wire until it melts, which opens the circuit.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true: a short circuit is live and neutral touching directly, and failed insulation is a common cause.
t: Recall the causes of a short circuit.

x: All three are correct: overloading comes from too many high-power devices, it draws high current that causes heating and fire risk, and a fuse or MCB cuts the circuit to protect against it.
t: Link overloading to its cause, effect and protective device.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Overloading occurs when too many high-power devices are used.
II. Overloading produces very high current, causing heating and fire hazard.
III. A fuse or MCB protects the circuit against overloading.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

x: A rectifier uses diodes, comes in half-wave, full-wave and bridge types, is used in power supplies and chargers, and converts AC to DC, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the parts and uses of a rectifier.

x: Magnetic brakes are used in trains, dynamic microphones turn sound into electrical signals, induction motors drive industry, and metal detectors find hidden metal, all by electromagnetic induction, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Match each induction device to its use.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Magnetic brakes
(b) Dynamic microphones
(c) Induction motors
(d) Metal detectors

List-II
(i) Industrial motors
(ii) Trains
(iii) Convert sound vibrations into electrical signals
(iv) Detect hidden metal objects

x: Nichrome and constantan barely change resistance with temperature, electrolytes lose resistance as they warm, and superconductors have zero resistance below the critical temperature, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-i.
t: Discriminate how resistance changes with temperature for each material.

x: A motor takes electrical energy, which gives the coil a torque that makes it rotate. Induced emf belongs to generators.
t: Discriminate motor from generator.

x: Generators produce electricity in power stations. Electromagnets serve cranes and MRI, and magnetic storage is used in hard disks.
t: Recall where each device is used.

x: Relays are electromagnetically operated switches, MRI machines use strong superconducting electromagnets, cranes lift iron scrap with electromagnets, and power stations use generators, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Match each device to how it uses magnetism.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Relays
(b) MRI devices
(c) Cranes
(d) Power stations

List-II
(i) Generators
(ii) Electromagnets that lift heavy iron scrap
(iii) Electromagnetically operated switches
(iv) Strong superconducting electromagnets for imaging

x: Metal detectors use EMI sensors: a nearby metal object changes the induced currents and signals its presence. Magnetic brakes, induction cooktops and dynamic microphones use induction for braking, heating and sound pickup instead.
t: Pick the device whose purpose is to detect something.
s: Which of the following devices uses electromagnetic induction to detect hidden metal objects?
